# Clip

> Clip is a free, open-source macOS menu bar tool for region screenshots with annotations, region screen recording (MP4 or GIF) and on-device OCR to the clipboard. It wakes on a double-tap of the ⌘ key. Requires macOS 14 or later. MIT License.

Clip has no upload, no account and no telemetry. Its only network requests are a manual update check when the user chooses Check for Updates: a HEAD request to its GitHub releases page and a lookup of the latest tag on jsDelivr, sent at the same time. It is pure AppKit, built with Swift Package Manager, and ships as a universal binary.

## Key facts

- Trigger: double-tap ⌘ anywhere; other actions get global shortcuts in Settings › Shortcuts
- Capture: window snapping, pixel-precise selection, origin and size label, multiple displays, scrolling capture
- Annotations: rectangle, ellipse, arrow, line, pen, highlighter, mosaic, numbered markers, text; editable with undo and redo
- Recording: selected region to MP4 or GIF with a pause/stop HUD
- OCR: Apple Vision on device, with a built-in PP-OCRv6 model (Core ML) taking over when Vision errors, finds nothing or takes longer than 1.5 s; Chinese and English by default, copied straight to the clipboard
- Toolbar: one bar; any tool on the bar, in the More menu or hidden, with dividers anywhere (Settings › Toolbar)
- Network: only the manual update check; nothing is uploaded
- Download: about 15 MB DMG (the OCR model accounts for most of it)
- Platform: macOS 14 or later; Apple silicon and Intel
- Price: free; source code under the MIT License
- First launch: not notarized by Apple; allow once in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Open Anyway, then grant Accessibility and Screen Recording

## How it compares

Checked 30 October 2026.

- Shottr: 2.3 MB, pay what you want with purchase reminders; scrolling capture and OCR but no screen recording; checks for updates and collects telemetry that can be turned off.
- CleanShot X: 48 MB, $35 one-time or $10 a month with Cloud Pro; the most features, with optional cloud uploads.
- PixPin: 127 MB, free with an optional membership, closed source; scrolling capture, on-device OCR, video and GIF recording.
- Clip: 15 MB, free and MIT-licensed, goes online only for a manual update check.
